subject: art-design
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

options: A small preliminary model of a sculpture
questions.explain: A maquette is a small-scale model made to plan and test ideas for a larger sculpture.

questions.q: Etching is a printmaking process that uses what to cut into a metal plate?
questions.explain: In etching, acid bites into exposed lines of a metal plate, which then hold ink for printing.

questions.q: Which paint is water-based and dries quickly to a permanent finish?
questions.explain: Acrylic paint is water-based, dries fast and becomes water-resistant once dry.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.

options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

questions.q: Which 3D technique is additive, building up a form from a soft material?
questions.explain: Modelling adds and shapes pliable material such as clay to build up a form.

questions.q: In a composition, what is the 'focal point'?
options: The main area that draws the viewer's eye
The darkest area of the picture
questions.explain: The focal point is the part of the composition that attracts the viewer's attention first.
The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: A 'hue' refers to which property of colour?
options: The pure colour itself, such as red or blue
questions.explain: Hue is the name of the pure colour, such as red, yellow or blue, before tints or shades are added.

questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
In the exact centre of the image
Around the edges of the frame
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.
